claims.statement: NFZ documentation says medical-service validation and verification use checks developed by NFZ headquarters and that challenged reports requiring correction should be corrected promptly.
The official provider portal documentation exposes verification status and CSV export, indicating that structured post-check data exists for reconciliation workflows.
Published NFZ central validation material includes explicit error codes and checks such as limits on billed services and duplicate waiting-list/reporting conditions.

contrary_evidence: NFZ publishes its checks and provides a provider portal, so an external product must improve preflight and prioritisation rather than merely restate errors.
Practice-management vendors may already implement many deterministic validations.
Some errors require contract or clinical judgement and cannot be safely automated.

economics.acquisition_route: Obtain de-identified prior submission and correction exports from three providers, quantify preventable failures, then partner with one billing consultant or software vendor for a paid shadow-mode pilot.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Five hundred provider accounts averaging 2000 PLN monthly would produce 12m PLN annual recurring revenue. At a mature 35% owner-cash margin, about 4.2m PLN per year could create more than 12m PLN of cumulative distributions in four mature years after reinvestment and taxes, without a sale assumption.
economics.founder_time: Constrain the first product to one benefit category and shadow mode at 3-4.5 hours/day; no automated submission or clinical coding changes, and employment continues until objective traction and runway criteria are met.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Once an export connector and rule set are stable, checks are automated; target 68-82% gross margin after update monitoring and high-touch exception support.
economics.payback: Target under 4 months from reduced correction labour and faster accepted claims, but monetary delay and denial baselines must be measured at each provider.
economics.pricing: Assumption to test: 2500-8000 PLN implementation and 900-3500 PLN per provider per month by contract and line volume; settlement specialists receive a portfolio tier.
economics.retention_or_repeat: NFZ reporting and corrections recur monthly, and accumulated rule/customer configuration raises switching cost; providers may churn if their contract ends.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A labelled mapping from NFZ codes and validation messages to successful correction sequences, segmented by contract type and software export, improves explanations and triage over time.
fingerprint.customer: Independent Polish clinics, rehabilitation centres and diagnostic providers with NFZ contracts but without a large dedicated settlement team.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Integrate with one smaller medical-software vendor, then distribute through healthcare accounting offices and settlement specialists who can manage many provider accounts.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Local connector or private-cloud service that ingests vendor exports, applies versioned public validations plus customer-specific consistency tests, explains errors, prioritises monetary exposure and records corrections; recurring subscription with assisted onboarding.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The provider finance or billing lead pays by NFZ contract and claim-line volume when a submission file is preflighted; existing spend is billing labour and the loss is delayed or challenged reimbursement.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Before a monthly statistical report or corrected invoice is submitted, thousands of service lines must be checked against central validations, contract limits and patient/reporting consistency rules.

founder_fit: Rules engines, anomaly detection and error prioritisation fit the founder's analytical and data-science background.
A medical-student partner can help decode terminology and observe workflows without acting as a reimbursement authority.
A local-first architecture creates a Polish technical moat while reducing sensitive-data exposure.
Software and accounting channels can deliver recurring accounts with limited founder networking.
risks: Outdated or incomplete rules could suppress valid claims or miss payable errors.
Health and reimbursement data demand strict access, retention and GDPR controls.
The product could drift into unauthorised coding advice if explanations are not bounded.
A dominant medical-software vendor could close export access or copy the feature.

structure.control_point: The last machine validation and monetary-priority queue before an NFZ report or correction is submitted
structure.critical_dependency: Timely, accurate implementation of NFZ validations and compatible exports from practice-management systems

thesis: Provide smaller Polish NFZ-contracted outpatient and rehabilitation providers a local-first pre-submission layer that applies current validation rules to exported claim lines, explains likely failures and assembles a correction queue. The buyer already pays billing staff and waits for accepted settlements; value comes from fewer avoidable corrections and faster cash, without replacing the official portal or making reimbursement guarantees.
title: NFZ Claim Preflight and Correction Queue
uncertainties: The prevalence and monetary value of preventable NFZ rejections among small providers are unknown.
Availability and stability of supported export formats must be verified vendor by vendor.
The best initial benefit category and whether providers will permit a local connector are untested.
Pricing, margins, channel economics and wealth projections are assumptions.
